previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paradoxical vocal fold motion disorder, hypertension due to primary hyperaldosteronism, type 2 diabetes, pseudotumor cerebri, and tobacco use was admitted for worsening dysphonia over three days, likely exacerbated by household chemical exposure and ongoing smoking. She had no airway compromise or respiratory distress. A neck X-ray showed no obstruction, and her oxygenation remained stable. She was managed conservatively with continued omeprazole for laryngeal reflux and as-needed bronchodilators. Her enalapril was increased to 10 mg daily for improved blood pressure control, and glyburide was doubled to 5 mg daily. She was cleared by her laryngologist for discharge with a same-day outpatient bronchoscopy planned to evaluate for subglottic stenosis. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up instructions.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ woman with a PMHx significant for chronic HAs (both 
migraines and pseudotumor cerebri), DM2, HTN, HL, GERD and 
likely primary hyperaldosteronism presented with a 10 day 
history of refractory and intractable HAs.
.

Neurology:
Patient has had numerous ED visits for this complaint and also 
presented on the day following discharge. Patient has both 
diagnoses of IIH as well as migraines and is unable to tell the 
difference between the two. She had a recent ED visit on 
___ where LP revealed an opening pressure of 29 with a 
large volume tap until a closing pressure of 20 cmCSF. This had 
some effect per patient. On this occasion, headache was 
migrainous sounding with throbbing right frontal / ___ 
headache with nausea and phono/photophobia and without features 
suggestive of high ICP / contribution of IIH. Examination was 
non-focal without papilledema and patient had full visual fields 
and normal EOM without diplopia. Of note, her headache was in 
the setting of decreasing her usual propranolol dose from 20mg 
bid to 10mg qd out of concern of bradycardia to ___ although the 
patient stated that this was a not unusual level of her heart 
rate. Patient also had hypertension which was partially 
controlled and was seen by endocrine below. We increased 
acetazolamide to 500mg bid and increased propranolol back to 
20mg bid given previous impact on headache but headache 
persisted. Given her likely transformed migraine and she was 
given valproate 750mg IV bolus with some improvement in 
headache. She had requested a short course of oxycodone at the 
time of discharge stating that only benzodiazepines and opiates 
relieve her headache and was given a prescription for 5x10mg 
tablets. She was discharged on ___ with headache clinic 
___ with Dr ___ this is not until ___. 
She re-presented to the ED on ___ with recurrent headache, 
nausea, vomiting and monocular diplopia and was treated with a 
further dose of IV valproate and 2g IV magnesium with 
supplemental oxygen and was discharged home with neurology 
urgent care ___.

Endocrine:
Patient has a long history of hypertension which started in her 
___. She was seen by endocrine as the diagnosis of 
hyper-aldosteronism had seemingly never been formally. They had 
felt, however that this is the most likely diagnosis given HTN 
from an early adult age and persistently low serum K. Patient 
was started on spironolactone for 1 day and unfortunately a 
pre-spironolactone level could not be added on. Spironolactone 
was stopped after this one day. Renin and plasma metanephrine 
levels are pending at time of writing. We added back enalapril 
10mg which was her previous dose, for HTN control. Patient was 
not able to finish 24hour urinary cortisol during this 
admission. She has endocrinology ___ and was instructed to 
stop enalapril  weeks prior to this appointment.
